wa_eldorado_peak_east_ridge.primary: Eldorado Creek climbers' path to Inspiration Glacier high camp

why.Late-spring snow cover (skis or boots): Late May and June, when snow covers the upper approach and the boulder field, and parties accept avalanche exposure for faster ground; ski parties also choose it for the descent.

wa_emerald_peak_west_route.primary: North Fork Entiat Trail #1437 to the meadow camp

why.Emerald Park trail from Lucerne: When coming from the Lake Chelan side by boat, or linking Emerald with Saska or other Chelan-side peaks, since it avoids the long drive and walk up the North Fork Entiat.

wa_energizer_bunny.primary: Aasgard Pass and the Core, to the left side of the south face

why.Snow Lakes and the lower Enchantments: Earlier in the season while Aasgard Pass is snowy, or for parties wanting to skip the loose scree grind, at the cost of about two extra miles and a thousand feet of gain.

wa_fifth_of_july_mountain_scramble.primary: Basalt Ridge crest to Fifth of July Pass

why.Entiat River and Larch Lakes: For a multi-day trip or loop, since it keeps to maintained trail with water and lets you camp at the lakes, though it is longer than the ridge line.

wa_flora_mountain_southwest_slope.primary: Devore Creek Trail from Bird Creek Camp over the Enigma saddle

why.Holden Village over Tenmile Pass: When linking Flora with Riddle Peak, or when finishing out to Holden after climbing from Stehekin; it is much longer than the Devore Creek line.

wa_forbidden_peak_west_ridge.primary: South face couloir to the West Ridge notch

why.Cat Scratch gullies (late season, once t: Late summer, once the couloir has gone icy, rocky and prone to rockfall, and the rock gullies to its west offer a surer way to the notch without a snow-to-rock transition.

wa_glacier_peak_frostbite_ridge.primary: North Fork Sauk to White Pass, then north

why.White Chuck River and Kennedy Ridge to t: Only if the White Chuck road and trail are ever rebuilt; since the 2003 flood it has been closed, so it is not a realistic choice and most parties take the Sauk route.
why.Suiattle River Road and the PCT via Milk: When the Suiattle River road is open and a party prefers the north side, though its trails are poorly maintained and the road has repeatedly flooded out.

wa_glacier_peak_kennedy_glacier.primary: North Fork Sauk and the crest trail north

why.White Chuck River and Kennedy Ridge to t: Only when the White Chuck road is repaired and open; it is the short historic way to the Glacier Creek camps but has been closed since the 2003 flood.

wa_glacier_peak_sitkum_glacier.primary: North Fork Sauk Trail and the PCT over Red Pass

why.White Chuck River Trail #643 (closed sin: Only if the road and trail are restored; it is the old, much shorter standard approach, but flood damage has closed it, so parties now walk in from the North Fork Sauk.

wa_golden_age.primary: Up the gully to its own ledge

why.Via the centre route's lower pitches: In dry summer conditions, when a party wants to climb more of the wall and does not mind carrying gear for the extra pitches instead of scrambling the gully to the ledge.
why.Via the right-hand cave route's lower pi: In dry summer conditions, for parties who want extra climbing and are happy with a longer leftward traverse across the wall to the shared ledge.

wa_gray_wolf_ridge_se_slopes.primary: Lower Maynard Burn Trail #816 over Baldy and along the crest

why.Royal Basin and the east face, for a tra: When turning the climb into a traverse or loop, finishing down to the Royal Basin trail instead of retracing the Baldy ridge, accepting steep loose ground.

wa_gunn_peak_southeast_route.primary: Barclay Creek climbers' path — summer line

why.Tailgunner couloir — snow-season line: Late spring, while the couloir holds continuous consolidated snow and avalanche danger has been judged low; once it melts out, the summer line is the right choice.
